rows.text: Memories shape a person's character, but the retention of memories is often selective: Optimists remember success, pessimists remember failure. But if setbacks are carved in stone and joys are written in sand, even the bravest becomes afraid of the future. Whether it was the result of an experiment or simply out of twisted amusement, the Memokeeper "Red Herring" anchored the greatest heartknots in the lives of 332 people and compiled them into a book. He recorded their setbacks, grudges, and regrets. The beautiful things in people's memories faded with the years, while the traumas persisted, and some of the affected individuals even forged blood feuds with one another. It wasn't until the Cremator "The Angler" burned away all the memories in the book that the farce finally ended.
